operations.comment: ; Baseball (Nintendo, 1984) -- NROM-128, commented ca65 source.
; ROMAtlas NES source; original bytes are local-only (image.nes).
; Physical layout: 16-byte iNES header, 16 KiB PRG (file $0010-$400F) visible at
; CPU $C000-$FFFF (and mirrored at $8000, unused by the code), 8 KiB CHR ROM.
; All code runs with the static NROM view prg_banks [0,1,0,1]; there is no banking.
; Program structure in brief
; - RESET ($C40B) clears RAM and enters the title screen. Nearly all game logic
;   runs as cooperative tasks: TaskCreate ($EB0A) queues a task slot with an entry
;   address, TaskSleep/TaskWaitFrame/TaskWaitList suspend the current task, and
;   the dispatcher (TaskEnd, $EB6A) idles with NMI enabled until NMI readies work.
; - NMI ($C046) flushes the PPU write queue at $0300, does OAM DMA, runs the
;   sound driver, reads both pads and (unless paused) creates the per-frame
;   FrameTask and wakes every task waiting on wait list 0.
; - Many subroutines take argument bytes placed directly after their JSR. The
;   helper GetInlineArgs ($E99A) arranges for the callee's RTS to skip them.
;   These argument bytes are emitted below as .byte/.word directives after the call.
; - Object slots: task slot numbers double as object offsets. Slot 0 is the ball,
;   even slots 2..$26 are the 19 on-field people (fielders, batter, runners).
;   Per-object arrays below are indexed by the slot number (stride 2 in RAM,
;   because positions are 16-bit). Positions are 8.8 fixed point world units.
; - Text uses the CHR font: tiles $00-$09 are digits, $0A-$23 letters A-Z,
;   $25 blank (see PPU string lists).
; Uncertain interpretations are worded tentatively in comments. Ranges the phase-1
; map leaves Unknown are emitted as raw .incbin with an explanatory note (none remain;
; the former Unknown byte at $E5F4 is generic Data by a user-directed fallback, see there).
; "No known caller" means no ROM-encoded reference was found; reachability is unknown
; (such routines are not claimed to be unused).
